Hello there! Welcome to Kitty Kitty Bounce Bounce!
Let’s learn how to play the game. First, navigation: to move around, press A/D or left/right arrow on your keyboard. Once you feel ready to launch Kitty, press spacebar or click the left mouse button - but launching Kitty is only possible in the gameplay view, in case you were surprised it doesn’t work right now.
Sometimes, the text you see on the screen is slightly too long - and this is where scrolling enters. Autoscrolling is on by default but you can change it - and the speed in which the text is scrolled - in the options. Press ‘O’ on your keyboard to open the options window at any time. If some part of the story scrolled too soon or you’re still faster than the auto scrolling, you can scroll up and down the text with either W/S button or the up/down arrows.
Once you’re ready to continue with the game, run Kitty into the green block on the right.

You might have noticed that breaking blocks can make them drop things. Let’s focus on those that have a big and long impact on your gameplay experience: paddles. They vary in sizes and bounciness so you might want to find which one suits your style of playing.
<sprite name="paddle">
Your default paddle: purple, balanced, and medium in size. Pretty comfortable, but it’ll neither help nor hinder your playthrough.
<sprite name="paddle2">
The fast boi: golden, bouncy, and a bit narrower than the default one. The extra bounciness and the size of this paddle might be demanding but definitely speed up your playthrough and adds some excitement to it!
<sprite name="paddle3">
Last but not least: blue, soft, and really wide. A safety net in the form of a cushion - it shouldn’t surprise you too much and it’s definitely a way to make your playthrough a little calmer.

Another two types of drops you should keep your eyes peeled for are:
 <sprite name="bomb">
and
<sprite name="serducho">
Can you guess what they’re for?
Yeah, the heart gives you another go in case Kitty slips past the paddle and you lose a life.
But the bomb! This one is pretty cool. Catch the drop and you’ll be armed with a bomb - and you can catch more than one at a time! Once you’ve got a bomb and Kitty touches the paddle, they’ll be automatically grabbing it and using it at the first block they boink against. As soon as the boink occurs so does the explosion!
And if you like the explosion, you’ll like the chain destruction that can be triggered randomly, more likely in the lower difficulty levels.

Lastly, there are the drops you can catch that will give you extra points.
<sprite name="5drop"><sprite name="10drop"><sprite name="15drop">
Breaking blocks on its own will reward you with points but you’ll find that points are a nice thing to have in abundance - especially if you ever find yourself in a pickle. Then, press “Tab” to open the shop and spend your hard-earned points!

Alright, that’s the last piece of advice, promise! Apart from a variety of drops, there’s also a variety of blocks and what they can do:
<sprite name="01"><sprite name="02"><sprite name="03"><sprite name="04"><sprite name="05"><sprite name="06"><sprite name="07"><sprite name="08"><sprite name="09"><sprite name="10"><sprite name="11"><sprite name="12"><sprite name="13"><sprite name="14">
These are your garden variety blocks, Kitty usually only needs to collide with them once and they break, you get the points and probably a drop, depending on the difficulty setting you chose.
<sprite name="invisible0"><sprite name="invisible1"><sprite name="invisible2"><sprite name="invisible3">
These take a couple of boinks before finally giving in and breaking. They begin at their most transparent and get more opaque the more damaged they are.
<sprite name="invincible">
These don’t appear too often and are unbreakable, hence their sinister appearance.
Now, all those blocks can be and sometimes are animated for some extra flair and challenge, hehe.
Have fun and thanks for playing Kitty Kitty Bounce Bounce!

Curious fluffy little Kitty found some cuddly fluffy balls of yarn. They were simply gorgeous! All rainbow-y and string-y, and funny smelling. But when bit, they tickled Kitty’s tongue in a stomach-turning way. Kitty quickly spat the colourful wool out of his mouth with disgust. Kitty tried snuggling with the yarn instead but his fur and the wool produced different types of electricity. It wasn’t a very nice sensation and it left Kitty’s fur all cranky.
Kitty decided he didn’t want to play with the yarn anymore but when he tried to leave, the yarn attacked him once again with a malicious zap in the butt! It was yarn or Kitty!
Pippity, poppity, gonna give you the zoppity!

Sleepy fluffy little Kitty was dreaming of his life. It was his favourite kind of dream because he loved spending time with his human outdoors with all his might! For the amusement of both parties Kitty was fighting a feathery monstrosity the human seemed to be operating when suddenly the house swallowed the human entirely, trapping them! Before Kitty had a chance to react a bush jumped on him and covered him completely, too!
Kitty couldn’t let anyone or anything separate him from his beloved human, even if just in a dream! With all his strength, he focused and thought really hard and realised he’s, indeed, in a dream. Having done that, he decided he was now in charge and his goal now was simple:
Free the Kitty, rescue the human!

Bored out of his furry mind, fluffy little Kitty was dozing off on the couch, enjoying the laziness of the lazy afternoon. Suddenly, his human entered the room, carrying a suspicious package. Kitty opened his eyes wider and got up to see what the human came up with this time.
Jumping from the couch to the bookshelf to the chest of drawers next to where the human was standing, Kitty felt the drowsiness leave his body and the excitement build up. Once on the counter, Kitty faced a glass bowl full of water with some weird thingies floating in it. Those were completely alien to Kitty but oh, so alluring at the same time! The golden one, the biggest of all, seemed to catch Kitty’s glances and glanced back at him, mockingly, blowing bubbles with its silly little mouth. Kitty wouldn’t let some yellow floating thing make fun of him.
You’re not going to float much longer, golden floatie.

Fluffy chubby little Kitty hasn’t felt energised for a long while. Whether it was the effects of winter gluttony or sitting by the fireplace all the time, Kitty felt like an overflowing pack of mayonnaise. Suddenly, a sunbeam appeared on the floor before him! Both Kitty and his human could instantly smell the sweet aroma of spring in the air. Apparently, the weather was nice enough to spend some time outside, so much so that the human decided to have a nice little picnic outside with Kitty!
All was cool and dandy for some time but then the human’s phone rang and Kitty was left to guard the food. Kitty wasn’t very happy to do so, having found a lovely spot in the sun, just perfect to fry in… Kitty was relaxed and fast asleep when suddenly some suspicious, and quite obnoxious, chomping woke him up! So rude! Kitty looked in the direction of that sound and found a mouse-rat snacking on the human’s precious cheese! Kitty couldn’t let that rodent keep that up.
It was devermination time!

Very adventurous and even more jet-lagged Kitty was looking around his new home, searching for the best place to become a sleeping ball of fur. The human had found this house some time ago and now moved in for a year, for job purposes, whatever that meant. Kitty was not amused at first, but soon enough he changed his mind: all the praise and extra snacks given to him very generously by all the new friends in the neighbourhood. Suddenly, the new surroundings were quite pleasing!
One day, as Kitty was walking around, exploring the ever-changing new house, he spotted some juicy, appealing-looking green thing sticking out of an even more appealing-looking ceramic thing. The very thought of devouring the green thing made Kitty’s fur stand up. And then pushing the ceramic thing down onto the floor… The sound of the crushing made Kitty’s whiskers tingle!
Chop, chop, push, push!

Sleepy thirsty fluffy Kitty left his human’s bed to have a little drink by the dripping sink. As he was stepping down the stairs, he noticed a weird red hue seeping from the living room to the whole floor. ‘That’s weird,’ he thought and went to the kitchen. Licking the water off the tap, he wondered to himself about many different things, forgetting about the red hue.
That was, at least, until the hue got a voice. It was scratchy and unpleasant and spoke in a way Kitty didn’t understand. What was obvious to Kitty, however, was that it was threatening. Threatening Kitty or his human - not quite sure but Kitty wouldn’t take any chances. With fur on his back fluffed up and ears down on his head, Kitty was in full-on hunter mode. He sneaked into the living room and realised that the enemy is… The TV? On TV? In it?
Regardless, Kitty’s gonna pull the plug!

Outdoorsy restless fluffy Kitty was taking a moonlit walk with his human and their partner. The weather was nice and breezy, the night was bright and calm, many others went out to spend some time in the open air. Kitty was sniffing and playing around when the weirdest sounds reached Kitty’s ears. He heard them first and started preparing to fight, while humans remained chatting carefree beside him.
Kitty was also the first to notice suspicious figures appear up in the sky. He hissed and jumped around and caught his humans’ attention - and just in time, too, as only seconds after they crouched down to his level abductions began.
Those humans who weren’t sitting or crouching were beamed up first. A whole fleet of peculiar-looking beam-shooting creatures hung lower and lower, closing in on Kitty’s humans.
Kitty’s gotta pew pew, before they get to beam beam.

Kitty felt groggy. The world seemed to either have too many dimensions or not enough of them. Some annoying constant bubbling and buzzing was attacking Kitty’s ears, drilling inside his head and making him feel that much worse. At one point, he thought he was so out of it he could see himself from outside of his body. There were many Kitties around him but each weirder than the last and none looked quite like Kitty usually did. Kitty was now groggy and confused. Not an ideal combination, if you ask him. Kitty shook his head once and again to get rid of confusion but the weird Kitties remained where they were.
It was then when Kitty decided that what cannot be fought with sense and sensibility should be defeated with some hard bonce bonking. Kitty was up for the challenge.
Let’s bounce-bounce.

Some time has passed since fearless warrior Kitty saved humanity from certain doom at the hands of clone-making aliens. Thanks to Kitty’s courage, he and his human were now invited to go around the world both to receive thanks and to help out with other issues they’d come across - no task was too small or too big. Those travels also helped Kitty’s human do their thing of talking to other humans!
One day, when Kitty was enjoying the sunset on his human’s lap a big rumble came from the mountains. The sky got grey and the air smelled of dryness. There wasn’t much time but Kitty had to do something heroic to save everyone once again.
Kitty didn’t want the mountain to come to Kitty, so Kitty had to come to the mountain.

Adventurous lordly Kitty has been all around the world over the past couple years. His human, who started as just his human, now made a name for themselves as some kind of big brain person, speaking to great crowds of other humans while Kitty naps on their desks to his heart’s delight. Kitty was happy to step down from the spotlight and make place for his human, and enjoy gentle pets from all kinds of humans.
During one of such gatherings, a huge ruckus burst out in the streets. The building was swiftly evacuated and just in time, too. As soon as the last person ran out onto the pavement, a gigantic flying lizard flew into a neighbouring edifice, sprinkling everyone with cement dust and small rubble.
Time for the danger noodle to meet even more danger meatball.

Seasoned serious Kitty was visiting some hot and dry place with his human. The climate felt nice for Kitty’s bones and joints that have been acting up for some time now whenever the weather changed. His human was glossy and wet most of the time they’d spend outside.
One day, Kitty and his human went to the big sandy place to look for some artefacts. Kitty didn’t understand much but was happy to accompany his human. They went into some structure and ventured into its labyrinth. Kitty didn’t like the smell of the air there and soon was dizzy from turning left, right, left, right…
Kitty found himself alone in an unknown room and heard buzzing. It wasn’t Kitty’s favourite sound and his whiskers tingled in anticipation of an attack.
Kitty knew that the best defence is offence.

Kitty was confused. He was sure he was elsewhere just a blink of an eye before and now… Now, he was standing on a moonlit hill. There was a lot of heavy fog around what seemed like crooked teeth sticking out of the ground. Kitty walked towards one of the closest ones and realised they weren’t teeth but pieces of various stones. A cemetery, he concluded.
Just as he did, a spectre appeared in the air above him. They spoke without making sounds or moving much but Kitty knew what the thing was telling him. Kitty did not agree with it and decided to fight for his right to spend more time with his human.
Nobody puts Kitty in the corner or wherever the spectre wanted to put him.

Old and wise, yet still fluffy, Kitty lay in the kitchen, soaking in the warmth of the afternoon sun in his favourite sunspot. His human bustled around, preparing food and occasionally dropping a scrap here and there—Kitty’s well-earned perks after a lifetime of adventures.
Kitty stretched, his joints creaking like a rusty gate. As his paws hit the cool tiles, something caught his eye. It was lying there. Unmoving. Kitty’s tail twitched, ears pricked up. His eyes narrowed. Was it friend or foe? The object stared back at him silently. Too silently.
Kitty’s battle instincts kicked in as he sized up the green menace. It was long. It was shiny. It was… unsettling. Kitty knew better than to let a potential threat stay so close to his human. He learnt a lot from all his years of defeating all kinds of foes.
That green log will be no exception.

Kitty followed his human into the pyramid, the dry warmth easing his stiff joints. The air was thick with dust, but Kitty didn’t mind. His human was off looking at strange rocks, and Kitty, as always, was on his own mission - guarding his human.
As they ventured deeper, Kitty spotted movement on the stone floor—a gleaming scarab beetle, scuttling around like it owned the place. Kitty stopped in his tracks, eyes narrowing, the fire of old battles rekindling.
The scarab’s shiny shell glinted in the low light, daring Kitty to act. It clicked its legs, taunting him. With a twitch of his tail, Kitty readied himself. His muscles tensed, prepared for a strike.
This pyramid isn’t big enough for the both of us, bug.

One frosty September morning Kitty woke up with a strong urge to go outside. He knew he wouldn’t go back so he fought with the feeling for a couple of days, bidding his farewells the best he could. He jumped on his human’s desk and looked them deep in the eyes while they were working. Kitty fell asleep being flooded with love and appreciation, which he hoped to take with him when he would leave.
Kitty knew he would never truly be ready to part with his human, as he knew they wouldn’t with him, either. What had to happen, had to happen, however, and Kitty preferred to leave before it did. His human would panic and run around looking for him for a month or two, then they’d hope he’d just found another loving home and he’s alright but after years pass, his human would finally come to terms with Kitty’s disappearance. At least that’s what Kitty hoped for, when he was sneaking out into his very last adventure.
After some walking, he got to his secret spot - close enough to feel at home, yet hidden enough so that he knew his human would never look for him there. He lay down. He closed his eyes and reminisced about the beautiful life he had with his human. All their glorious adventures and shenanigans, each lovely evening and lazy afternoon.
Kitty’s breathing slowed down and so did his little heart. In his final moments, he wished to one day be reunited with his human or, at the very least, for them to love and be loved like Kitty did them - and they Kitty.

Itty bitty ginger Kitty found himself in a pickle. He could feel he was being carried around but the cosy darkness surrounding him didn’t allow looking around. When the Kitty container was put down on the floor and the cosy factor was removed from over Kitty’s head, the air vents and portviews became visible, letting blinding light in. Once the gates opened, Kitty ran out into the big glare, finally escaping his cushiony jail and promptly beginning the exploration.
This new environment was rather exciting, full of new shapes, colours, and scents. Once out in the wild and with his sight returned, Kitty turned around to face his kitty-napper. He found two people staring back at him, lovingly.
He stepped closer to them and suddenly felt his fur stand up on his back. An adversary was near. Kitty looked around but saw nothing - until he looked behind himself. There it was - his temporary prison, ready to swallow him once more, who knows for how long this time!
Kitty had to make sure it never had another chance.

Itty bitty ginger Kitty was utterly bamboozled.
After freeing him, humans put Kitty in their litter-box room with his own litter box and some soft blankies. That on its own wasn’t too confusing but then they started opening and closing the door with a big cat glaring at Kitty from behind it.
Once their weird ritual was finished, Kitty was free to leave the white-tiled, big smelly prison. He wasn’t too interested in getting to know his new surroundings anymore, believing that eventually he’ll end up imprisoned again. Instead, he focused on the black giant that peeked into the human litter box before. The giant was soft and smelled a lot like the humans but wouldn’t engage with Kitty, even when cordially invited to play. He didn’t mind Kitty lying next to him, though, so that’s what Kitty did. Kitty was ready to fall asleep when, suddenly, the giant leapt into the other room. Without thinking much, Kitty followed closely behind. There was this enticing aroma coming from there, growing stronger the nearer Kitty was to the humans.
Were those humans made of food?

Itty bitty chonky Kitty was feeling a little peckish. Licking his paws, he was imagining they were covered in the liquid of happiness he always finds in his food bowl on the chewy bits. Then, suddenly, out of nowhere an adversary appeared right in front of him! It was hopping and bobbing, so full of feathers and noisy metal balls! Mocking him from a safe distance, withdrawing whenever Kitty tried to swat it. Kitty had to really put his back into it now!
Overcome with rage, Kitty hadn’t noticed who was controlling the enemy all that time. The clarity of mind returned only when he stopped attacking, almost ready to admit his defeat. It was then that he realised the betrayal - tiny humans played a trick on him! Kitty decided to take his revenge on the soft, weirdly shaped pillow the tinier of the humans often hugged. This insult demanded a blood spill!

Itty bitty chonky Kitty was enjoying the warmth of the weird window beside which his humans were sitting. The crackling and irregular movement that came from within made Kitty feel some primitive calm he rarely experienced. Lying on top of his humans made his energy restoration accelerate further, even faster than his soft little body was prepared for!
Suddenly, overcharged, Kitty felt overcome with his primitive instincts and enraged! He needed an outlet for his frenzy! Alas, Kitty was shooed away from his humans who apparently didn’t appreciate his aggressive love biting. He then directed his focus onto a more sturdy target - and one that couldn’t run away or fight back!
The new target proved to be a worthy opponent, resisting the might of Kitty’s teeth. It was time to show the log who’s the boss and go all out!

Plumpy chompy chunky Kitty was resting after his most recent primal rage session full of love biting and sharpening claws when, out of nowhere, he felt something touching his fur ever so slightly. Out of the bigness of his heart, he let it slide and felt very mindful, very demure about his self-control and mercy.
Soon enough, however, he felt the feeling again, then again, and again! His peaceful nap went out of the window and so did his peaceful attitude. Kitty opened his eyes, now full of wrath, and looked around. Searching for some silly human’s hand teasing him, he realised who’s the enemy pestering him so persistently. Pesky flying little specks of dust and fluff. Kitty was about to revoke their pilot licence!

Plumpy chompy chunky Kitty had spent the whole week feasting on some juicy festive leftovers and illegal snacks sneakily snuck under the table by his humans’ visitors. That beautiful, bountiful moment in his life ended - and way too early - however, and a new one started, much to Kitty’s dissatisfaction.
This new period was a colourful but also very noisy one. Every time a distant “BOOM” went off, Kitty would jump up and blindly attack anything in his reach. He tried hiding from the sound but couldn’t. The sheer panic he felt settled in his heart, his throat and in his humans - in their skin, with the help of his teeth and nails, of course.
Eventually, unable to find the right hideaway, Kitty found himself at the end of his wits and decided to take matters in his own paws. It was time to fight those noisy colourful bursts - into oblivion, if need be.

Plumpy rowdy chompy Kitty woke up one day feeling especially primal and wild. He decided he had been imprisoned far too long. His blob of a body, however stunning, felt like a sour reminder of his inaction against the unjust confinement. At first he just jumped around, trying to escape out of this wretched maze his humans call ‘home’.
He huffed and puffed as he climbed all of the windowsills he could spot, hoping to find one of the windows open. He’d tried doors before but his humans - those sneaky jailors! - always catch him at the last second and throw him back into incarceration.
After a while, he found the portal to his freedom in the bathroom. The amount of acrobatics he had to do to get all the way up and the bravery to actually jump outside should have already earned him all the independence he could wish for, and yet - another obstacle awaited him.
Kitty fretted not, for he was ready to tangle.

Itty bitty misplaced Kitty was wandering the unknown for quite some time now. He hadn’t expected that the outside world had no designated nap places or scratchies behind the ear - not even juicy snacks to be found in clean bowls! Kitty was outraged, then he was sad, and then afraid. The last feeling was a novelty and not a welcome one.
There were noises and lights Kitty had never experienced before and, if it was up to him, he wouldn’t anymore, oh no, no no, NO. The sheer variety and intensity of them made Kitty very confused and very agitated. He wanted to fight, he wanted to flee, he wanted to eat, he wanted to sleep.
With so much happening at once, Kitty didn’t know where to put his paws first. In a flash of mental clarity Kitty realised that the most dangerous enemy at that moment was the confusion itself.
Time to go up that spiral for a change!

Tired placid famished Kitty roamed the streets for days on end, losing weight but not gaining too much fitness in its place. The adventure his heart so desired before was now a big complex chore that could be summed up simply to ‘stay alive’. How mundane!
Other cats didn’t seem too empathetic to his humanified background and not only wouldn’t share their food with Kitty but would even bully him until he’d run away - they would even smack him! Outrageous!
Kitty was smart enough, however, to understand that those other kitties weren’t really his enemies and didn’t deserve to feel his wrath so he didn’t whack them back but rather stayed away from them. Thanks to that he avoided so many silly fights and came up with a genius idea - if he returned to his humans and let them take care of all his needs, he wouldn’t have to work so hard!
The streets were a maze but Kitty was ready to un-lose himself in it!

Itchy nauseous hurty Kitty was beside himself with emotions when his humans finally found him. Of course, he was just about to reach them himself, without any help, but it was nice to be carried instead of having to walk on his own legs.
He ate to his heart’s content, threw up, ate more, threw up again, and only then decided he caught up with the meals he had skipped during his adventure. Then, out of nowhere, his humans picked him up, put him into a weird but comfy container, and took him somewhere.
Kitty heard some commotion, conversations, and sounds of distress of other animals - and when the blanket was lifted from his temporary little house, he even smelled them. There was also another aroma in the air but before he could put his claw on it, some strange human began to handle him. That itself was more annoying than anything but then an enemy appeared.
It was sharp but Kitty was sharper.

Healthy plumpy fluffy Kitty was bored out of his mind. The fatigue and injuries of his escapade had long been treated and forgotten and the yearning for excitement that still lived in Kitty’s heart remained, ever so strong - growing stronger each day he lay dormant.
The safety and comfort of life in the house stood in stark contrast to the lively and risky time on the streets he kept reminiscing, dozing off after an especially big dinner.
Looking for some stimulant, Kitty walked around the house, avoiding the other cat cautiously. With his street experience, the dangerous glimmer in the older Kitty’s eyes made Kitty’s ginger fur stand tall on his back with fear.
Eventually, Kitty came across an unsupervised and very prohibited object he could tap over the edge of the counter. It’s better than nothing.
Let the hunt begin!

Happy frisky orange Kitty decided it was time to take another go at being a wildling. Feeling much more prepared than ever before, more determined, too, he didn’t waste any time planning and instead decided to just wing it.
Like before, he went around the house first but his humans learnt a lot from his past escape - all windows were closed or guarded. Kitty decided to play the long game and stalked the doors he knew sometimes opened. Afternoon came and went, Kitty’s heart still set on getting out, only leaving his station to eat.
Finally, late in the evening, when his humans were talking to visiting humans, Kitty’s chance finally appeared. The visiting humans, preoccupied with talking or just inept in guarding the escape routes, gave him just enough space to bolt out the door!
Now, Kitty was faced with the fence. It’d been reinforced but so had Kitty. Freedom!

Kitty managed to leave the house once again, huzzah! Having learnt the power of jumping onto taller and taller objects, he finally defeated the fence and jumped over it! And all that despite his humans having installed extra precautions against him escaping! How silly of them, ha! As if their puny acts of defiance could ever stop his ferocious need for freedom!
When Kitty’s soft paws first touched the rough and dirty concrete pavement, he suddenly remembered all the bad times he had had on the streets. Being the wild and ferocious Kitty that he was, shaking off the doubts and the fear that began to set in his heart, he set off onto the new adventure.
He’d been dreaming about it, he was so prepared, he will do better this time. He won’t let the other cats bully him again, he’ll hunt like no one had ever hunted before, and he’ll show everybody how capable he really was!
His resolve and bravado were cut short when he stepped out onto the pavement and all the noises flooded his brain. Kitty began to panic, his fur stood up, his breath shortened, his eyes darted from one place to another. Hoping to get away from danger, Kitty hurried in a random direction, craving peace and quiet, even at the price of being bored again - but instead, he found his untimely end when one of the noise-makers ran into him.
Kitty didn’t feel the impact. Kitty didn’t feel regrets for having left his safe home. He only felt cold. The kind of cold that can only be cured by a warm hug from his humans. In his last moments, Kitty hoped to one day feel it again.

Nimble lively little Kitty was patrolling her perimeter. She was still very new to life and even newer to this place. Granny let her out of the house for the day so Kitty decided to spend her time getting to explore and map out everything she’d have to guard from now on.
The day was warm and the air was fragrant with the scent of wet grass waking up from the winter slumber. Kitty was so petit, she had to jump to see over the taller chunks of grass but thanks to that she quickly spotted a potentially dangerous curiosity not far from her!
She jumped and jumped, until she was close enough to leap forward straight into battle. She readied herself and hopped! It’s Kitty’s turf now, no strangers allowed!

Lively curious cautious Kitty was out and about. Granny had left the house to go to another one she visited regularly but forgot to leave Kitty’s bowls out before, so Kitty was ever so peckish. To better ignore the pangs of empty mouth, she set off onto exploring her perimeter again.
She wandered into one of the buildings surrounding the courtyard. The walls and roof of this one were made of wonky boards with gaps in-between letting in just enough light from the outside for Kitty to see everything. Some more or less fresh straw lay everywhere and made the air smell warm and funky. It was nice and quiet there, though!
Kitty felt as though this place was a perfect nap hideaway and was about to try it out when she heard something weird! Some squeaking and rustling. All the doziness suddenly left Kitty’s body and she realised her life’s calling - and she’s about to respond!

Sleepy happy little Kitty was woken up by a cock’s crowing at the sunrise. She looked around and saw granny still asleep. She looked even more around and noticed the can with treats for granny’s grandchildren open. Kitty had tried to look inside that can ever since she first saw it but granny was adamant that it was a special thing for human children only.
Now, that it lay open and granny couldn’t stop Kitty, Kitty hopped on the table and slowly approached this mysterious container. Inside were very colourful things that sounded funny when Kitty swatted her little paw at them. She swatted and swatted and then one of those strange objects suddenly jumped out of the can!
Granny moved around, grunting like she always did minutes before getting up. Kitty had to get rid of the evidence she messed around in the forbidden can - and quick!

Lively cheerful little Kitty was prancing around in grass after checking out each and every corner of her perimeter. She was especially frisky that day, having successfully hunted a few invaders and ready to take on more! The barn that she previously deemed a perfect nap spot wasn’t that but rather a battlefield - though that day even that place was silent.
Kitty wandered into one of the calmest corners of the courtyard to climb on the outside windowsill to watch the road behind the fence. This windowsill was her second favourite place to idly spend time, since she had a view on the inside of the house where granny liked to sit and the even more outside, onto the road and the neighbouring houses.
Just as she was about to jump up, she spotted an entity she’d never seen before. It was flying, seemingly with a goal in its mind. Kitty had to shoot it down, just in case. Her airspace had no place for a UFO, even a cute one!

Lively cranky petit Kitty woke up feeling damp. She knew this feeling to only appear when a cold wetness lingered around. She checked the stove and to her dissatisfaction found it lukewarm instead of hot, the way she liked it the most. Something was amiss and Kitty set off onto investigation, while granny put more coal in to warm up the house.
Kitty walked around, inspecting each room very carefully. They were all similarly chilly in a wet way that finally made Kitty go outside. Then, both to Kitty’s surprise and disdain, she realised the root of the problem - snow was falling again!
Winter was not welcome to return - Kitty had to chuck her out, one snowflake at a time!

Lonely anxious petit Kitty was wandering around the house. Granny had a little fall on a puddle of ice before, and moaned and groaned, then the neighbours came, then some strangers in glaringly orange clothes, and then they all left, and now Kitty was all alone.
The rooms were weirdly quiet and cold despite the stove still warming the whole house rather well. Kitty tried to entertain herself and use this as an opportunity to do all the forbidden things she couldn’t with granny around. But without granny around nothing felt too nice so Kitty quickly dropped being a hooligan.
That is, until she spotted some pieces of coal that had escaped the stove. Those posed a fire hazard. Granny needed to have a house to come home to - Kitty was going to bring some heat to coal!

Lonely confused petit Kitty was worried about granny. Ever since her fall on ice, Kitty hadn’t seen granny and to make matters worse granny’s relatives that visited weekly now abducted Kitty to live with them!
Kitty explored her new environment but despite her efforts, she never once left the house. At first, she didn’t mind it all that much. Her perimeter wasn’t anywhere near anyway and sleeping usually made time fly by faster, so that’s just what she did all day, ad nauseam.
The sun came out again and warmed the numerous plants in Kitty’s favourite room. They became very fragrant and all was fine and dandy until one of them started to smell so strong Kitty couldn’t ignore it anymore. Well, plant, get ready to become a little fertilizer!

Anxious somber petit Kitty was lounging in her favourite room in the house of her kidnappers. She couldn’t stop thinking about granny, with each passing day becoming more and more worried that they’d never meet again.
Her kidnappers seemed to notice the decline in Kitty’s mood and tried giving her tastier snacks, making her food increasingly fancy and rich, her pillows were softer and cushier the gloomier Kitty was. She only got a little livelier when they brought a blanket from granny’s room.
That’s when the little humans who would normally pester and chase her around her perimeter whenever she was trying to do her job came up with an idea. They whipped out a cat toy from somewhere and tried to play with her. That was a sweet gesture.
Kitty decided to humour them.

Determined desperate petit Kitty was out and about looking for granny. She hadn’t seen her for weeks now, spring became summer, and autumn was at the door. As soon as Kitty left the house, however, she found herself in not just an alien but also a very smelly environment.
She tried to navigate it, following her instincts, but they did not lead her out into a clearing and then fields that would take her back home, to granny, hot stove, her perimeter, tall grass, and all the rest of things she so loved.
Negative thoughts and emotions boiled inside Kitty’s heart the longer she was circling around, unable to get where she wanted to. Eventually, all of it erupted when out of nowhere, a bottle rolled onto Kitty’s leg. Something had to break - better bottle than Kitty’s heart!

Ecstatic chatty petit Kitty was finally reunited with granny! She had to use this weird cold device to walk and each step was an effort but she was back at home, and so was Kitty!
Kitty meowed about all of the things that had happened in her life during their separation, how lonely she felt, how she wouldn’t survive being without her, what fun they’d have now that they were together forever.
Granny didn’t pay enough attention, in Kitty’s opinion. She wasn’t cooing and responding to Kitty, focusing instead a bit too much on that walking aid. It had to go.

Giddy chatty petit Kitty was telling granny all about her time out in the garden when she was waiting for granny’s return. All the new bugs she had never seen before, all the mice she’d annihilated, the naps she was going to have and where as soon as granny fed her her breakfast.
Granny responded, walking all the way to the kitchen that was also her bedroom, and the two had a nice little chat. Suddenly, granny yelped, and put her hand to her chest. She fell back onto the bed and Kitty quickly looked at what scared granny so much.
It was big, visibly weathered in battle, and ready for another. Kitty was happy to oblige!

Kitty and granny spent another three years together. It was a glorious, joyous time full of affection, delicious treats, and carefree naps in many secret napping spots. Each day was warm and fuzzy in a way that touched Kitty’s heart. Kitty was to granny what granny was to Kitty - they supported each other like a young tree leaning on a stake to grow straight up.
When old age caught up to granny and she collapsed and withered away soon after, Kitty hoped, despite her own prognoses and worst fears. She hoped and imagined so hard that granny would return, and if Kitty knew how, she would bop her nose against granny’s to make her all better.
But once taken by the orange-clothed people, granny never returned. Kitty was, once again, taken to the strangers’ house. She tried staying for as long as she could but as seasons came and went, she couldn’t wait anymore. She escaped and found her own way back home.
It was silent and cold in a way a place can only be when no one had been inside for a long time. Granny’s scent was almost completely gone and Kitty realised that they’d never meet in this life again. She walked her perimeter one last time, just in case, then lay on her favourite windowsill to take her last nap, hoping she’d dream of her time with granny.
